fixes.explanation: Close, baker, but the LORD says the opposite. He says, "Even their children remember their altars and Asherah poles by the green trees and on the high hills." So the children haven't forgotten these things. They remember them.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "Even their children remember their altars and Asherah poles by the green trees and on the high hills." The children aren't forgetting a thing, and I think that's what makes this verse so heavy.

Egypt is a famous place for slavery, baker, but this verse never says it. The LORD says, "I will enslave you to your enemies in a land that you do not know…" He doesn't name the land here. He says it's one they don't know.
I wish that were the word, baker, but it's not. The LORD says, "…you have kindled My anger; it will burn forever." So no burning out soon. This is one of the heavy parts.
Right on, baker. The LORD says the man who trusts in mankind "…will be like a shrub in the desert…" A shrub out in the desert. Hardly a picture of someone who's doing well.
A tree against a wall could at least get some shade, baker. But the LORD says the man who trusts in Him is "…like a tree planted by the waters…" Waters is the word the verse uses.

I'd love to say I know my own heart, baker, but the verse says otherwise. It asks, "Who can understand it?" Then the LORD answers, "I, the LORD, search the heart; I examine the mind…" He's the one who searches.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, "Like a partridge hatching eggs it did not lay is the man who makes a fortune unjustly." A partridge sitting on eggs she did not lay. That's the picture of a fortune made unjustly.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says, "In the middle of his days his riches will desert him, and in the end he will be the fool." So the money doesn't last. The fortune walks out on him.
Yes, baker. They say, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!" They want it to show up right then. And the one praying says they keep saying it to him.

You got it, baker. The prayer says, "Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame." It's the cry of someone being persecuted. I think it's a hard prayer, and the text just lets it stand.
